subtype: Approach: relies on a lucky routine on exam day [Action]
passage:
Rain was hammering the road when Parth left for the last paper of the term. He had done what he always did: two nights of past-paper questions, a list of formulas pinned above his desk, and the same blue pen in his pocket.
The bus was late, so he ran the last stretch and slowed at the old temple wall. He pressed his palm against the wet stone for two breaths. His shoulders dropped.
"Every time?" Shreya asked, catching up under the shelter.
"Every time," said Parth. "It doesn't do the sums, though."
Inside, he wrote the first answer with the blue pen, steady, and it was the formulas that got him through the question on rates.

qa.q: What does Parth press his palm against before the paper?
qa.a: Parth presses his palm against the wet stone of the old temple wall for two breaths.

qa.q: What does the temple wall do for Parth's mood?
qa.a: It calms him, since his shoulders dropped after two breaths at the wall.

qa.q: What could help Parth stay calm if he could not reach the wall?
qa.a: Parth could take two slow breaths with the blue pen in hand, because the calm seems to come from a short pause, and his real preparation is the past papers and the formulas.

qa.q: How does Shreya seem to see Parth's ritual?
qa.a: Shreya asks 'Every time?' with curiosity, not mockery, and hears Parth say the wall does not do the sums.

grounding: A teenager uses a lucky pen and a wall touch to feel calm on exam day while also studying.

subtype: Approach: relies on a lucky routine on exam day [Action]
passage: On board exam mornings in their Jaipur colony, Madhav's routine never changed. He checked his pencil box for the blue pen with the chewed cap, the one he'd used since Class 8. On the walk to the bus stop, he stopped at the little Hanuman temple on the corner and pressed his palm to the cool stone wall for a moment. His father, Jagdish, walking beside him, never teased. Madhav had tried to explain once: "It doesn't make me pass. It makes my hands stop shaking." The night before, he had done three past papers and gone to bed at ten. Now, with the pen in his pocket and the wall's coolness still on his palm, he got on the bus breathing slowly.

qa.q: How many past papers did Madhav do the night before?
How does the temple wall routine make Madhav feel?
qa.a: It makes him calmer; he says it makes his hands stop shaking, even though he knows it doesn't make him pass.

qa.q: What does Madhav's routine do well?
qa.a: It calms his nerves while the real preparation, the three past papers and an early night, does the work.

qa.q: How does Jagdish see his son's ritual?
qa.a: Jagdish seems respectful and understanding, never teasing, because it helps Madhav stay calm.

grounding: A teenager keeps a lucky pen and touches a temple wall before exams to calm down, while still studying, so the ritual supports effort.

passage:
"Ronak, why do you always stop here?"
"It's my exam thing, Yusuf. I touch the temple wall. Every exam since Class 7."
Gurleen laughed. "And the green pen? You've had that pen forever."
"Same pen, same wall." Ronak pressed his hand to the stone. "Okay. Done."
"Does it work?" Yusuf asked.
"It doesn't write the answers, if that's what you mean. I did the whole revision sheet last night, and two mocks this week."
"Then why do it?"
Ronak thought. "When I touch the wall, my stomach calms down. Then I can think."
Gurleen nodded slowly. "Like my deep breaths before a match."
"Exactly." Ronak clicked the green pen. "The studying is the work. This just gets me in the door."

qa.q: How many mocks did Ronak do this week?
How does touching the wall make Ronak feel?
qa.a: It calms the knot in his stomach so he can think clearly.

qa.q: Why does Ronak's routine help rather than replace effort?
qa.a: He does the revision sheet and mocks, and uses the ritual only to calm down before the exam.

qa.q: How does Gurleen come to see Ronak's ritual?
qa.a: Gurleen laughs at first, then understands it's like the deep breaths she takes before a match.

grounding: A teenager keeps a lucky pen and touches a temple wall before exams to stay calm, alongside real study.
